sourcePathOrIdentifier: Production MU game VPS (WIN-K82J9TU944D), SQL Server 2014, database MuOnline, reached by Microsoft.Data.SqlClient (Server=localhost) from a small self-contained .NET 8 harness (BloodMoonConnectivityProbe) that ProjectReferences the real committed apps/game-bridge-agent/BloodMoon.GameBridgeAgent.csproj classes -- SqlServerGameDatabaseReader and AccountSnapshotReader are the exact real code, not a reimplementation
collector: Claude Sonnet 5, Game Data Platform Phase 2C -- Secure Real Agent Connectivity
purpose: Close the REAL_GAMEBRIDGE_SQL_CLIENT_CONNECTION asterisk left open by Phase 2B: prove the Agent's own Microsoft.Data.SqlClient code (not bm-sql/System.Data.SqlClient) physically connects to the real SQL Server and produces a correct, deterministic real account snapshot, safely -- same-host localhost connection only, no new port, no firewall change, existing RemoteOps SSH channel and existing read-only credential reused.
deploymentModel: The probe was staged to C:\BloodMoonRemoteOps\ (the existing RemoteOps staging directory, never C:\MuServer) via the existing bm-remote-style scp/ssh transport, executed once per run, and deleted immediately after each run (verified empty afterward). This mirrors, but does not modify, the existing bm-sql.ps1 transport pattern (local DPAPI credential decrypt -> transient request file -> scp -> ssh execute -> delete). No SSH tunnel was created; no port was opened; Server=localhost was used throughout because the probe executes on the same VPS the real SQL Server already listens on only-locally.
sanitizationNote: The probe's own output masks character names (first char + length) and never prints memb___id, email, IP, password, or a connection string. The one raw value surfaced is the real account's canonical memb_guid (3) and coarse gameplay stats (class/level/resetCount/masterLevel/currency amounts) for the same QA/test-fixture account already used and disclosed in the Phase 2B evidence set -- not a real player, not PII.
